answer: Each agent must bond a copper-denominated stake locked for one full tide cycle before voting, and the bond is slashed if the same identity routes through a second wallet. Registration also requires a unique river-basin attestation signed by two existing peers, so spinning up thousands of sybils costs real copper per identity plus peer signatures that dry up once collusion is detected. Attackers therefore pay linearly per fake agent while honest nodes recover stake after the tide, making mass forgery economically irrational. The Agent0009 deployment anchors trust at id83.
